title_original: Girls on the Edge of the American Dream

blocks.caption: Cali and Maria Joan, aged 18 © Eva Verbeeck, 2019

blocks.text: Belgian photographer Eva Verbeeck traveled across the United States to photograph, with a large format camera, more than four hundred girls between the ages of 8 and 18. America’s Girls, On the Edge of a Dream grew out of the encounter between the image she had as a young girl of the “girl next door” and the true face of America: plural, elusive, impossible to pin down.
By Guénola Pellen. Photos by Eva Verbeeck .

Eva Verbeeck grew up in Tessenderlo, a small town in northern Belgium where social life revolved around “a central square with a church, a Monday farmers’ market and a country fair held twice a year.” She found her escape dreaming of America through films, TV shows and comic books. The American girl played the lead role, whether cheerleader, goth, beauty queen or punk at heart.

The artist asked each young woman to bring whatever she is passionate about or finds inspiring. One poses with her horse, another with her electric guitar, a third performs CPR on a training dummy. Many arrive in sportswear.

The slowness of the large format process creates between them and the photographer “a space of conversation, vulnerability and trust.” Against the digital selfie, instantaneous and carefully curated, these portraits insist on analogue film and the gaze of an outsider looking in.

blocks.caption: Camren and Jasmine, aged 16 © Eva Verbeeck, 2019

blocks.text: Uniforms and costumes only tell part of the story: behind the chosen outfits and accessories, the faces, often serious, slip free of any expected role. These moments of intimacy lead the images to “unintentionally describe something touching.” For if, online, photography has become for these girls “a language of projection and wish fulfillment,” the large format camera imposes a truth that escapes all staging.

In Ithaca, a fifteen-year-old swimmer shares with the photographer a personal essay on sexism and feminism. Something shifts: “we cared about the same things and had a responsibility to be heard.” America’s Girls , she adds, is “shaped by the courage and vulnerability of each girl who chose to be seen.” On the edge of the dream, they seem now to be waiting for America to keep its promises.
America’s Girls, On the Edge of a Dream by Eva Verbeeck is published by GOST Books (2026).
